thesis: CRISPR Therapeutics is the gene-editing pioneer behind Casgevy (exa-cel), the world's first approved CRISPR/Cas9 medicine, commercialized with partner Vertex Pharmaceuticals (CRSP owns 40% of profits and losses). With roughly $2.4B in cash and a deep, de-risked pipeline spanning in vivo cardiovascular editing (CTX310/CTX320), CAR-T immuno-oncology and autoimmune programs (CTX112), and regenerative medicine for diabetes, CRSP is a validated platform company. But Casgevy's launch is slow, cash burn runs near $400M a year, and the value depends on binary clinical readouts — a high-conviction but high-uncertainty story best sized as a speculative position.

drivers: Casgevy commercial ramp accelerates as authorized treatment centers scale globally and ex-US reimbursement broadens, turning CRSP's 40% profit share positive
In vivo pipeline (CTX310 ANGPTL3, CTX320 Lp(a)) delivers durable, best-in-class LDL and Lp(a) reductions, validating a repeat-dose-free cardiovascular franchise with a multi-billion-dollar TAM

CTX112 CD19 CAR-T posts strong data in B-cell malignancies and autoimmune disease, and the diabetes and regenerative programs advance — re-rating CRSP from single-product biotech to multi-asset platform

base_case.assumptions: Casgevy uptake grows gradually but remains modest through 2026-2027; in vivo and CAR-T programs generate encouraging but not definitive data; CRSP stays pre-profit and continues burning ~$400M a year, funded by its ~$2.4B cash pile. The stock drifts toward the ~$67.78 analyst consensus target as pipeline milestones de-risk the platform.

risks: Casgevy commercialization stays slow due to complex ex-vivo logistics, long cell-collection-to-infusion timelines, and payer friction, keeping CRSP's profit share negative
A clinical setback or safety signal in the in vivo or CAR-T pipeline resets platform expectations
Persistent ~$400M annual cash burn eventually forces a dilutive raise, pressuring the share count and price

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 results — Casgevy patient starts, authorized treatment center activations, and cash-burn trajectory
Clinical data updates for in vivo programs CTX310 (ANGPTL3) and CTX320 (Lp(a)) targeting cardiovascular disease
CTX112 (CD19 CAR-T) data readouts in B-cell malignancies and autoimmune indications
Casgevy label and geographic expansion — additional treatment centers and ex-US reimbursement milestones with Vertex
Progress in regenerative medicine, including CTX211/VCTX-series programs for type 1 diabetes

key_risks: Slow Casgevy commercial ramp given ex-vivo cell-therapy complexity, long vein-to-vein times, and payer reimbursement friction
Binary clinical risk across the in vivo (CTX310/CTX320) and CAR-T (CTX112) pipeline — a single failure can reset the thesis
High cash burn (~$400M/year) and no near-term path to profitability, raising eventual dilution risk despite ~$2.4B cash
Dependence on Vertex partnership economics for Casgevy (CRSP holds only 40% of profits and losses)
High short interest (~22% of float) and biotech sector rate sensitivity amplify volatility
Competition in gene editing (Intellia, Beam, base/prime editing) and in cardiovascular RNA/gene therapies
